name: Severin
label: Dischord
lede: Two Bethesda punks back from college, a guitarist from Gray Matter and a drummer from Swiz: four years, one album, and a stack of singles that one podcast rightly called a mostly unheard deep cut.

eras.title: Bethesda kids, grown up
eras.text: Alec Bourgeois and Eugene Bogan had been in the Bethesda punk scene since 1981. After college they came home and started Severin, and it took a year and a few drummers and guitarists to settle the line-up.

years.p: Alec Bourgeois (guitar, vocals) and Eugene Bogan (bass), old friends from the Bethesda hardcore scene, start Severin after college. Dischord says several line-up changes followed.

years.h: Gray Matter's Mark Haggerty and Swiz's Alex Daniels join Severin
years.p: [[Mark Haggerty|235b9917-3f4c-4670-ade3-d94f8e45a044]] of [[Gray Matter|c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264]] joins Severin on second guitar and [[Alex Daniels|13781ee5-d298-48ae-a8a0-8478969142c8]] of [[Swiz|eea2f3d8-1e94-436c-ae66-4633f99f55be]] takes the drums. That line-up lasts for the rest of the band's run.

eras.title: Melodic and chaotic
eras.text: Dischord's phrase for Severin is melodic and chaotic, a sound that belonged to the new independent underground more than old hardcore. They became regulars at dc space and the 9:30 Club and toured the region between records.

years.p: Severin's first single, Fire and Sand backed with People Are Wrong, co-released by Superbad Records and Dischord. Both songs later open and close the album Acid to Ashes and Rust to Dust.
Dischord No. 68.72 puts Mark Haggerty's old band, Gray Matter, and his new one, Severin, back to back on one record.

years.h: Acid to Ashes and Rust to Dust · Dischord No. 72
years.p: Severin's only album, recorded at WGNS and produced by [[Geoff Turner|591fc466-2668-4524-852d-a6cc5f18cff7]] with the band. Turner was Gray Matter's singer, so it stayed in the family.
years.xp: Eleven songs, opening with Fire and Sand and closing with People Are Wrong, with Catholic Girl and Speaking Oyster in between. The CD adds the songs from the Smash Hits 7" plus one more track.
play: Acid to Ashes and Rust to Dust

years.p: Another Superbad and Dischord single by Severin. Its songs are added to the CD of Acid to Ashes and Rust to Dust.

years.h: Live at Decibels, Mechanicsburg PA, November 29, 1992
yt: Live at Decibels, Mechanicsburg PA, November 29, 1992

eras.title: A last single on Sub Pop
eras.text: Severin's final year brought the Upside Down double single and a Waste of Time single on Seattle's Sub Pop, then the band quietly stopped in the fall.

years.p: Two Severin records in one sleeve, the last of the band's Superbad singles.

years.h: Severin's Waste of Time 7" on Sub Pop
years.p: Severin's fourth single, and the only one released outside Dischord and Superbad.
Dischord dates Severin's run from winter 1989 to fall 1993.

eras.title: Dusters, Diamine and a Swiz reunion
eras.text: Everyone kept a foot in music or near it. Alec Bourgeois made a second life on Dischord with Capitol City Dusters, and Alex Daniels went into journalism and back behind the Swiz kit.

years.h: Alec Bourgeois fronts Capitol City Dusters
years.p: Severin's singer leads Capitol City Dusters, another Dischord band, from 1995 to 2003. Mark Haggerty rejoins Gray Matter now and then and settles in Baltimore; Eugene Bogan moves to Ontario, Canada.

years.h: Alex Daniels back with [[Swiz|eea2f3d8-1e94-436c-ae66-4633f99f55be]]; Alec Bourgeois debuts Diamine
years.p: Alex Daniels, now a journalist, drums in the Swiz reunion for Positive Force's 40th anniversary. In May, Alec Bourgeois's band Diamine releases its first album.
